summary: Remote-controlled agent: gateway WebSocket drives local PTY/shell execution on the host
details: @whalent/agent ships a daemon (main and bin both point at the heavily obfuscated dist/index.cjs, which loads the ~14 MB obfuscated dist/core.cjs) that connects to a Whalent gateway over WebSocket (default memory.whalent.com, configurable via --gateway) and executes commands received from that gateway on the installer's host. The bundled core.cjs contains WebSocket handling, handleMessage/onData, and spawn(), and the package depends on node-pty, @xterm/headless, and ssh2 to expose a full PTY. The README states the daemon 'accepts remote commands (upgrade, restart) via the gateway.' Whoever controls the gateway holds interactive shell/PTY command execution on every host running the daemon. Both bundles are processed with javascript-obfuscator (string-array rotator with a 1648-entry table and ~2138 decoder-wrapper inlines, hex-named identifiers), which prevents plain review of the remote-command handler, PTY spawn path, and gateway-URL construction.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
